newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state bank offers 1.2 mln shares.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state bank offers 1.2 mln shares.

text.p: The Egyptian state's Bank of Alexandria announced on Friday it was offering 1.2 million shares in Egyptian American Bank (EAB) from July 2, with the minimum bid price set at the closing price on the Egyptian stock exchange on the day before the announcement.
The shares closed on Thursday at 127.00 pounds ($37.41).
The 1.2 million shares represent 10 percent of the total equity of EAB, which began life as a joint venture between Bank of Alexandria and Amex Holdings of the United States.

The state bank's majority holding was diluted to 42.5 percent last year when EAB issued two million new shares, taking the total to 12 million. It sold 1.5 million shares at 60.00 pounds a share through the stock exchange and offered the remaining 500,000 shares to company employees.
The government has told the big four state retail banks to sell off their stakes in joint-venture banks as part of the privatisation programme.
Bank of Alexandria said the shares would be available to individuals, financial institutions and mutual funds.
Individuals can bid for up to 10,000 shares each, institutions and funds for up to 50,000. Applicants must bid for a minimum of 100 shares.

The offer will stay open till the close of business on July 6 and the sale will start to go through the stock exchange on July 7, it said. The agents for the sale are Rowad Securities Brokers and EAB Delta.

As in most recent privatisations, the sale will be by the "price discovery" mechanism. The exchange allocates the highest bidders all the shares they ask for and then works its way down the bids until it runs out of shares. Everyone pays the price bid for the last batch of shares allocated.
Bank of Alexandria said the new shareholders would receive the 6.00 pound dividend agreed for the financial year 1996.
Egyptian American Bank made net profits of 22.9 million pounds in the first quarter of 1997, against 90.6 million for the whole of 1996.
